title: [YouPass Collect] - UK Household Technology Adoption in 1997-2001
prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of households with different kinds of technology in the UK from 1997 to 2001. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the proportion of households in the UK that owned five different types of technology between 1997 and 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, most technologies experienced growth in household ownership throughout the period, though the rate of increase varied considerably. CD players remained the most prevalent technology across all years, while DVD player ownership fluctuated notably, declining initially before recovering by 2001.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding technologies with steady growth patterns, CD players were owned by 60% of households in 1997, the highest figure among all categories. This technology maintained its leading position throughout the period, with ownership rising gradually to 80% by 2001. Similarly, computers were present in 40% of homes initially and experienced consistent growth over the following years, reaching 70% in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for technologies that saw more dramatic changes, telephones started at the lowest level in 1997, with only 20% ownership, identical to their 1998 figure. However, they subsequently experienced remarkable growth, surging to 75% by 2001, nearly quadrupling from their initial level. A comparable trajectory was observed for Internet access, which began at merely 10% in 1997 and climbed sharply to 60% by the end of the period, representing a sixfold increase. Meanwhile, DVD player ownership displayed a different pattern, starting at 26% in 1997 but declining to 15% in 1998, its lowest point. After this trough, it recovered substantially, rising to 50% by 2001.
